title: Grade 6 Science — Wed, Jun 18
description: Changes Around Us — Day 3 of 5: Irreversible changes
subject: science

questions.question: An irreversible change is one that ___.
options: Cannot be reversed to give back the original substances
questions.explanation: An irreversible change cannot be reversed — the original substances cannot be recovered once the change has occurred.

questions.question: Burning of a candle is irreversible because ___.
options: New substances (CO₂ and water vapour) are produced
questions.explanation: When a candle burns, wax reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water vapour — new substances, making it irreversible.

questions.question: Cooking an egg is irreversible because ___.
options: It changes the egg's shape only
Heat causes permanent chemical changes in the proteins
questions.explanation: Heat causes the proteins in the egg to denature (undergo chemical change permanently). This cannot be reversed.

questions.question: Curdling of milk is an example of a ___ change.
questions.explanation: Curdling is a chemical change — bacteria produce lactic acid, permanently changing the milk. It is irreversible.

questions.question: Which of these is an irreversible change?
questions.explanation: Baking bread involves chemical reactions that permanently change the dough. Bread cannot become raw dough again.

questions.question: Growth of a plant is ___.
questions.explanation: Growth involves complex chemical changes in cells. A plant cannot un-grow — it is an irreversible chemical change.

questions.question: Rusting of iron is irreversible because ___.
options: A new substance (iron oxide) is formed that cannot easily revert to iron
questions.explanation: Rust (iron oxide) is a new chemical compound. Converting it back to iron requires complex industrial processes.

questions.question: Ripening of a mango is a ___ change.
questions.explanation: Ripening involves chemical changes in sugars, acids, and pigments — a ripe mango cannot return to being raw.

questions.question: Mixing cement with water is irreversible because ___.
options: A chemical reaction produces hard concrete that cannot be reversed
questions.explanation: Cement + water undergoes hydration (a chemical reaction) forming concrete — a new, hard substance that is irreversible.

questions.question: An irreversible change always involves ___.
questions.explanation: Irreversible changes involve the formation of new substances with different properties from the originals.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an irreversible change?
questions.explanation: Melting of butter is reversible — cooled butter solidifies again. Burning, digestion, and fermentation are irreversible.

questions.question: Lighting a firecracker produces ___.
options: Light, sound, and gases — an irreversible chemical change
questions.explanation: Burning a firecracker is an irreversible chemical change — it produces light, sound, heat and gases.

questions.question: Digestion of food in our body is ___.
questions.explanation: Digestion involves chemical reactions (enzymes breaking down food into simpler molecules) — irreversible.

questions.question: Which of these involves a permanent change in material properties?
questions.explanation: Burning leaves produces ash and gases — new substances with different properties. This is a permanent irreversible change.

questions.question: Once iron has rusted, the best approach is to ___.
options: Reverse the rusting by adding water
Remove the rust by scraping/coating — reversal to original iron is not practical
Re-melt the iron easily at home
Cool the iron to restore it
questions.explanation: Rusting is irreversible under normal conditions. Rust can be removed and the iron re-protected, but cannot simply be 'un-rusted.'
